Subject: Reserved capacity proposal — pricing under GPU volatility

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the product overview last week. Atlas is interested in a 24-month reserved capacity commitment to support inference for our assistant product. Before we proceed to SOW language, procurement and legal need clarity on a few items related to GPU-market volatility: 

- Would Redwood accept a defined indexation clause if spot/market GPU pricing moves >25% year-over-year?
- How do discount tiers change if committed SKUs shift between generations mid-term?
- Can we get a short runbook for escape/hardship events (e.g., sudden hardware price shocks)?

Attached is our RFQ and expected forecast for Q4–Q1 usage. Please include any proposed contract language and a point of contact for finance approval.

Regards,
Emma Klein
Senior Counsel, Atlas AI
procurement@atlasai.com

Emma —

Appreciate the details and the forecast. Short answers up front: yes to a limited indexation clause (conditional), and yes to tier adjustments for SKU migrations with careful compatibility mapping. That said, we need to align internally on how we operationalize an indexation/hedge so we can give you concrete language.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal sync between Sales/Finance/Infra to run 3 pricing scenarios (base, +25% GPU cost shock, -15% GPU deflation) — Marcus can lead the modeling.
2) I’ll draft two contract options: (A) fixed per-token pricing with an annual GPU-index clause capped at +/-20%; (B) flexible tier pricing with credits/offsets for verified market shocks and a quarterly reconciliation.
3) If either option looks acceptable, we prepare a 14-day pilot at a blended rate while legal redlines.

I attached our working cost model and a short note on implementation tradeoffs. Can Marcus and Grace confirm availability for a 45-min sync this week?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Attaching preliminary scenarios. High level:

- Base: GPU amortized cost steady -> blended reserved unit price aligned to committed SKU mix. Net margin impact: -4% relative to spot-only baseline.
- Upside shock (+25% GPU cost YoY): if we absorb 50% of shock to avoid churn, margin hit ranges -12% to -18% depending on utilization; pass-through only above a 30% threshold keeps margin within -8% worst-case.
- Deflation (-15%): opportunity to provide one-time credits or expedite model upgrades; offers favorable economics and improves gross margin by ~6%.

Attachments: gpu_price_scenarios.csv (scenario table), quick_notes.txt.

Recommendation: Offer Option B (flexible tiers + quarterly reconciliation) with a capped indexation band at +/-25%, and a defined executive escalation for >25% movement. This balances customer predictability and our exposure.

Marcus Lin
Senior Product Finance Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: gpu_price_scenarios.csv
From: aditya_rao

Cc: emma.klein@atlasai.com, laura_bennett, grace_oconnor
Date: 2026-10-04T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed contract language + pilot option (Atlas AI)

Emma —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is a redline with two options and implementation notes:

Option A — Fixed blended rate with annual indexation review:
- Annual tech-index adjustment capped at +/-20% with mutual review; material swings (>30%) allow for mid-term reconciliation or conversion to Option B.

Option B — Flexible tier + quarterly reconciliation (recommended):
- Price tiers map to committed SKUs; if a SKU migration is required, Redwood will map to an equivalent SKU and provide a one-time credit calculated from usage delta.
- Quarterly settlement statement; pass-through for cumulative GPU cost movement >25% in a quarter triggers a 30-day review and an executive decision.

Pilot: 30 days, up to 10% of committed volume at a blended pilot rate. If pilot proceeds, finance will do a pre-invoice holdback to reconcile after quarter close.

We welcome legal redlines; I can route an approved final to DocuSign once we converge. HubSpot link and proposed SOW attached for reference.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_contract_redline.docx
Related: https://hubspot.company/deal/ATL-2026-092
From: emma.klein@atlasai.com

Cc: procurement@atlasai.com, ops@atlasai.com

Subject: Re: Proposed contract language + pilot option (Atlas AI)

Aditya / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Legal prefers Option B with the quarterly reconciliation, and requests the following changes before we sign:
1) Narrow the trigger to "cumulative GPU cost movement >22% over a 90-day period" (we can accept 22% rather than 25%).
2) Add an audit right for Atlas to verify market index inputs for one reconciliation per 12-month window.
3) Pilot: please confirm how credits will be calculated if a SKU migration during pilot causes a cost delta.

If Redwood agrees to 1) and 2) we can sign the SOW and run the pilot while finalizing exact credit math. Please send a DocuSign link and the pilot SOW.

Emma Klein
Senior Counsel, Atlas AI
procurement@atlasai.com
